From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

# Project Kestrel — Buyer-side review of Seller Update and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Preliminary note on the Seller's preamble.** The statements that the positions "were settled at principal level", "reflect the agreed commercial bargain" and are "marked FINAL and not intended to be re-opened" are the Seller's assertions, not evidence of anything. We have no instruction from the Wattlebridge deal team that any of these points are agreed. Treat every position below as open. The "market context" paragraph is also self-serving: the ranges quoted are at the seller-friendly end and ignore the specific risk profile revealed by DD (undischarged debt, unconsented key customer, unresolved IP transfer, live privacy incident).

---

## SPA-N-001: General liability cap
- **Seller:** 20% of price (AUD 4.8m) for general Warranty Claims (cl 12.1).
- **Buyer wants:** General cap of 100% of price, or at minimum 50%; cap applies only to general business warranties; fundamental, tax, IP and specific indemnities sit outside it.
- **Recommendation:** Reject 20%; counter at 100% with fallback to 50%. *Reason: the known-issue exposure alone (Riverlark 3.2m, Bluefen 3.6m revenue at risk, Ironquay, incident) could exhaust a 4.8m cap before any unknown breach is covered.*

## SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket
- **Seller:** De minimis AUD 25k; basket AUD 250k; excess-only (deductible) recovery (cl 12.2).
- **Buyer wants:** De minimis AUD 10k; basket AUD 120k (0.5%); tipping basket (first-dollar recovery); related claims aggregated; thresholds not applied to fundamental, tax or indemnity claims.
- **Recommendation:** Reject deductible basket; counter with tipping basket at ~0.5% and de minimis AUD 10k. *Reason: a deductible plus a 25k per-claim floor on a 24m SaaS business with many small contracts quietly writes off a large slice of realistic losses.*

## SPA-N-003: General claims time limit
- **Seller:** 18 months from Completion; and any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly excluded (cl 12.3/13).
- **Buyer wants:** 24 months for general warranties (covers two audit cycles); claim preserved if notified in time and proceedings issued within 6–9 months after; no "applies to all Claims" default.
- **Recommendation:** Counter at 24 months and delete the catch-all sentence. *Reason: 18 months gives only one post-completion audit, and the catch-all would silently drag tax, title and indemnities into the short period.*

## SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties "for administrative simplicity".
- **Buyer wants:** Fundamental warranties (title, capacity, authority, no encumbrances, share capital) capped at 100% of price, no de minimis/basket, 6–7 year limitation period.
- **Recommendation:** Reject outright. *Reason: "administrative simplicity" is not a reason to accept recovering only 20% of price if the Buyer does not get good title to what it paid for.*

## SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out
- **Seller:** None stated; limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance "apply to all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3/12.8/20.5), which would purport to cover fraud.
- **Buyer wants:** Express carve-out: no cap, threshold, time limit, non-reliance or exclusive-remedy clause applies to claims arising from fraud, dishonesty, wilful concealment or wilful misconduct of the Seller or its officers.
- **Recommendation:** Insert the carve-out; non-negotiable. *Reason: a limitation that purports to cover fraud is unlikely to be enforceable anyway but the absence of the carve-out signals a problem and invites litigation over scope.*

## SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope
- **Seller:** General disclosure of the entire data room (DD-002 to DD-012), the Accounts, statutory registers and all publicly searchable records (Disclosure Letter 1.1–1.2).
- **Buyer wants:** Only specific, fair and reasonably detailed disclosures in the Disclosure Letter qualify the warranties; data room disclosed only to the extent a matter is fairly disclosed from the face of the document; no disclosure of public registers generally; certain warranties (title, Riverlark, Bluefen, Ironquay, incident) not capable of being qualified by disclosure at all.
- **Recommendation:** Reject general disclosure; require specific disclosure against numbered warranties with a "fair disclosure" standard. *Reason: a blanket data-room disclosure plus clause 1.4 ("nothing admits anything") lets the Seller disclose a problem without disclosing that it is a problem.*

## SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier
- **Seller:** No claim for any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including anything "discoverable" from the data room or public records (cl 8.3).
- **Buyer wants:** Delete. At most, limit to matters actually known by a short named list of Buyer deal-team individuals, and only where the knowledge derives from the specific disclosures in the Disclosure Letter.
- **Recommendation:** Delete cl 8.3 entirely. *Reason: "discoverable" imputes constructive knowledge of every document and public search, which combined with N-006 would eliminate the warranty package.*

## SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent
- **Seller:** Reasonable endeavours only; consent "treated as satisfied" on delivery of counterparty's written consent (cl 3/6.3). Disclosure Letter item 2 admits no final consent and no evidence that cl 11.3 conditions are met.
- **Buyer wants:** Unconditional written Bluefen consent (and satisfaction/waiver of 11.3 conditions) as a Condition Precedent in a form approved by Buyer; Seller to use best endeavours; Buyer walk right or price adjustment if not obtained; no deemed satisfaction language.
- **Recommendation:** Make it a hard CP with Buyer approval of form; delete deemed-satisfaction wording. *Reason: ~30% of FY26 revenue (AUD 3.6m) depends on a consent the Seller has not yet obtained.*

## SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility
- **Seller:** Release "to be provided following Completion" (cl 2/7). Disclosure item 3 confirms AUD 3.2m outstanding, not repaid, no discharge.
- **Buyer wants:** Full repayment and executed deed of release/discharge of security (plus PPSR discharge) delivered **at** Completion, funded from the purchase price via the funds flow; payoff letter from Riverlark pre-Completion; Seller indemnity for any residual amount.
- **Recommendation:** Reject post-Completion release; require repayment and discharge as a Completion deliverable with price deduction. *Reason: the deal is debt-free/cash-free, and a 3.2m secured facility left in place after Completion is the Buyer's debt with the Seller holding the money.*

## SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses
- **Seller:** AUD 420k closing bonuses are "a matter for the Seller", not itemised in funds flow. Disclosure item 5 confirms they are payable on Completion and continued employment, with on-costs unaddressed.
- **Buyer wants:** Bonuses plus superannuation, payroll tax and all on-costs treated as Transaction Expenses / debt-like items deducted from the price in the funds flow (or paid by Seller pre-Completion with evidence); Seller indemnity for any shortfall; schedule of who is paid and when.
- **Recommendation:** Add as a price deduction with gross-up for on-costs and a specific indemnity. *Reason: the obligor is the Company, so unless deducted, the Buyer is funding the Seller's transaction bonuses.*

## SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity
- **Seller:** Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment (AUD 180k) and "considered adequate" (cl 11.1). Disclosure item 4 confirms DD-004 cl 7.3 conditions IP transfer on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee; no receipt or assignment in data room.
- **Buyer wants:** CP or Completion deliverable: evidence of cleared payment of all SOW3 fees and an executed confirmatory IP assignment from Ironquay; uncapped (or price-capped) specific indemnity for any loss from Ironquay asserting ownership or the Company not owning the Project Materials, not just the 180k.
- **Recommendation:** Expand the indemnity to cover title-to-IP loss and make payment plus assignment a Completion deliverable. *Reason: the real risk is not the 180k fee but that the Company does not own the software it sells.*

## SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident
- **Seller:** "Preliminary operational matter", not material (cl 4.6/Sch 6). Disclosure item 6 confirms ~1,240 personal records sent to an unintended external address, access/notification status unknown.
- **Buyer wants:** Specific indemnity (outside cap, basket and general time limit) for all costs of investigation, OAIC notification, individual notification, regulatory penalties, customer claims and remediation; pre-Completion obligation to complete investigation and make any required notification; warranty that no other incidents exist; Buyer sign-off on incident response before Completion.
- **Recommendation:** Specific indemnity plus pre-Completion investigation covenant. *Reason: a known incident involving external disclosure of personal data cannot be fairly disclosed away as "not material" while its scope is admittedly unknown.*

## SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals
- **Seller:** Three renewals at AUD 110k each (330k) are ordinary-course operating costs. Disclosure item 8 does not say whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.
- **Buyer wants:** Clarify whether these are committed pre-Completion liabilities; if so, treat as accrued/working capital or debt-like items in completion accounts (or locked-box leakage); confirm termination rights and that the three are not a single split contract; cost not borne twice.
- **Recommendation:** Require specific disclosure of status and bring into the price mechanics if committed. *Reason: DD-008/DD-011 need to be read together and the Seller's "ordinary course" label is unsupported by its own disclosure.*

## SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller:** One regime for everything; limitations apply to all Claims "unless expressly stated otherwise" (cl 12.3/13, 9.3/12.8/20.5).
- **Buyer wants:** Clearly separated claim categories with distinct caps and time limits: (i) general warranties; (ii) fundamental/title; (iii) tax warranties and tax indemnity; (iv) IP warranties; (v) specific indemnities (Riverlark, Ironquay, incident, bonuses); (vi) fraud. Indemnities and tax outside de minimis/basket.
- **Recommendation:** Restructure Schedule of limitations into a category table. *Reason: the Seller's single-bucket drafting is the mechanism by which N-001 to N-003 are made to swallow the entire protection package.*

## SPA-N-015: Title verification
- **Seller:** Title evidenced by the Company's own share register at DD-012. Disclosure item 10 notes the Buyer has not completed its own verification.
- **Buyer wants:** Independent verification before signing: ASIC company and PPSR searches, review of share certificates, constitution, register of members and any shareholder agreements, confirmation no options/convertibles, confirmation Harbourglass itself has no security over the shares (particularly in favour of Riverlark). Title warranty unqualified by disclosure.
- **Recommendation:** Instruct searches now; do not rely on DD-012. *Reason: a company-maintained register is not independent proof, and Riverlark's security may extend to the shares.*

## SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms
- **Seller:** "Settled under the general regime" (20% cap, 18 months, basket).
- **Buyer wants:** Separate tax indemnity (pre-Completion tax, uncapped or at price, no basket, 7 years / statutory period plus 6 months); IP warranties (ownership, no infringement, open-source compliance, contractor assignments) with cap at price and 3–5 year period; both outside the knowledge qualifier.
- **Recommendation:** Treat as open and table Buyer's tax indemnity and IP warranty schedule. *Reason: nothing in the Seller's package actually addresses tax or IP terms, so "settled" means "not drafted".*

---

## Priority order for the mark-up
1. **Completion mechanics with cash consequences:** Riverlark (N-009), bonuses (N-010), Bluefen CP (N-008), Ironquay deliverables (N-011).
2. **Structural protections:** category separation (N-014), fundamental regime (N-004), fraud carve-out (N-005), delete cl 8.3 (N-007), specific disclosure (N-006).
3. **Economic terms:** cap (N-001), basket (N-002), time limit (N-003), tax/IP (N-016).
4. **Confirmatory diligence:** title searches (N-015), incident scope (N-012), Sandbar status (N-013).

Happy to turn this into a redline of the specific clauses or a short issues list for the principals.
